about.title: About
about.content:
About
I’m Phan Nguyen Huong Le (Valerie). I build reproducible statistical tools and data pipelines that help bridge experiments and theory in neuroscience. My work lives at the intersection of biostatistics, machine learning, and systems for reproducible analysis: I care about principled models, clear code, and workflows that let scientific teams scale analyses without losing interpretability.
During my master’s training I focused on preprocessing and statistical analyses for neural data, developing code and documentation to make experiments more reproducible and analyses more robust. I enjoy translating messy, high-dimensional recordings into concise results — whether that means a defensible model, a visualization that clarifies a phenomenon, or a pipeline that repeatedly reproduces a result across datasets.
Interests:

Computational neuroscience (neural coding, dynamics, population analyses)
Biostatistics and hierarchical / Bayesian modeling
Reproducible workflows: Docker, CI, literate programming
Data visualization and explainable ML

If you’re interested in collaboration, open-source tooling, or data for reproducible neuroscience/ biostatistics, I’d love to talk.

CV / Publications: Resume

experience.title: Experience
experience.content:
title: “Experience”
slug: “experience”
description: “Positions, roles, and academic appointments”
Experience
R/Shiny Developer — Rutgers University
June 2025 – Present | New Brunswick, NJ

Built an interactive Shiny application under Dr. Han Zhang and Dr. Philip He’s guidance to visualize hypothesis graphs and redistribute test weights dynamically for multiple testing procedures.
Collaborated on extending the open-source trialsimulator R package, improving usability and reproducibility for clinical trial simulations.
Designed features for node/edge editing, JSON import/export, enabling flexible experimental design.
Engaged in iterative development with faculty feedback, focusing on accessibility for applied statisticians and biomedical researchers.

Directed Reading in Causal Inference
June 2025 – August 2025 | New Brunswick, NJ

Studied CBPS, AIPW/DR estimators, overlap/trim rules, and matching vs weighting methods, mentored by Dr. Nicole Pashley.

Imaging Data Analyst — University of Pennsylvania / CHOP
July 2024 – Present | Philadelphia, PA

Developed and deployed nnU-Net v2 pipelines on HPC clusters (Slurm/GPU) for pediatric brain tumor segmentation.
Implemented Monte Carlo Dropout with 20 inference passes per case to generate uncertainty maps, supporting clinician quality assurance.
Processed and curated 100+ GB of multi-sequence MRI data with automated ETL, artifact logging, and reproducibility checks.
Contributed to AutoSurv pipeline integrating radiomics (1.2k+ features/patient) and clinical data; applied KL-PMVAE + LFSurv models and DeepSHAP interpretability, achieving 10% higher concordance than Cox baselines.

Research Assistant — Social Perception Lab
Sept 2023 – May 2024 | New Brunswick, NJ

Performed data cleaning and transformation for psychometric scale evaluation studies (Likert-type responses).
Applied Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) in R to assess construct validity and model fit.
Contributed to literature review and synthesis on measurement reliability and bias in social psychology, mentored by Dr. Lee Jussim.
Collaborated with senior researchers to interpret CFA results and refine scale design for ongoing projects.

Research Assistant — ABUSA REHAB Health Psychology Lab
Jan 2022 – May 2023 | New Brunswick, NJ

Conducted participant phone screens and managed data collection for smoking and stress intervention studies led by Dr. Teresa Leyro and Dr. Samantha Farris.
Processed heart rate data using HRV and PRV software to extract physiological stress biomarkers.
Supported clinical research protocols by maintaining participant logs, preparing data for statistical analysis, and assisting in literature review.

Data Science Intern — IDX Exchange
Location: New York, NY

Ingested and cleaned 2.3M MLS rows from 8 data sources into analytics tables; automated daily refresh with 99.5% success.
Trained an XGBoost AVM for home values with geo features (schools/transit/parks, neighborhood indices, age/reno flags), cutting RMSE 18% and reaching MAPE 7.9% on 5-fold CV (R² 0.71 → 0.77).
Deployed a home-value estimator API (p95 180 ms, 99.9% 30-day uptime) and integrated outputs into the property search module.
Built Tableau market dashboards across 42 counties; adopted by 3 product teams, reducing ad-hoc reporting time 60%.

Quantitative Research Mentee — JPMorgan Chase & Co.
Location: New York, NY

Engineered market-data ETL in Python (yfinance) to date-partitioned Parquet with schema/type checks and daily ingestions; ran 1M+ Monte Carlo stress paths, reducing VaR error by 8%.
Built forecasting/pricing components: LSTM improved equity prediction accuracy 12%; vectorized Black–Scholes pricer increased throughput 15%.

projects/biostats-toolkit.title: Biostatistics toolkit
projects/biostats-toolkit.content:
Biostatistics toolkit
An opinionated set of R and Python utilities for model fitting, reporting, and reproducible analysis pipelines. Includes helpers for hierarchical/Bayesian modeling, plotting standards, and reproducible reporting templates.
Highlights:

Reusable model wrappers and diagnostics
Templates for reproducible reports (R Markdown / Jupyter)
Unit tests and example analyses

projects/neural-data-analysis.title: Neural data analysis toolkit
projects/neural-data-analysis.content:
Neural data analysis toolkit
Pipelines and reproducible analyses for spike and imaging datasets. Includes preprocessing, quality control, and example analysis notebooks to reproduce published figures and exploratory analyses.
Key features:

Reusable preprocessing pipelines (spike sorting wrappers, imaging preprocessing)
Example notebooks demonstrating population analyses and visualization
CI-friendly tests and Dockerized workflows for reproducibility


title: “Neural data analysis toolkit”

Neural data analysis toolkit
Short description: Reproducible pipelines for preprocessing and analyzing electrophysiology and calcium imaging data. Includes automated QC, spike-sorting wrappers, and visualization modules.
Technologies: Python, numpy, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, MNE, custom wrappers.

projects/shiny-app.title: Interactive R/Shiny app for multiple testing
projects/shiny-app.content:
Interactive R/Shiny app for multiple testing
An interactive Shiny app developed with faculty collaboration to visualize hypothesis graphs and redistribute test weights dynamically for multiple testing procedures. Features JSON import/export, node/edge editing, and dynamic visual updates.
Details:

Built with R/Shiny and integrated into reproducible unit tests
Deployed internally and used as a demo for TrialSimulator
Designed for accessibility to applied biomedical researchers
